segments: The seventeenth dynasty.
The Arab kings.
[Möngke] Khan was sending.
Now Möngke Khan commanded
that from all the armies in the east and in the west, two persons out of every ten should go.
And from among the princes he sent with him a younger brother of his named Subetei Oghul;
and from Batu's side, Balaghai son of Sebaqan, and Qutar Oghul, and Quli, with numerous forces;
and from the domain of Chagatai, Tegüder, his grandson;
and from the side of Checheken (Chichek?) Bagi, sister of the Khan, Buqa-Temür, with the army of the Oirats;
and from the countries of Cathay (Khitai) they brought a thousand households of engineers (mangonel-men) and naft-throwers.
And ahead of the forces was sent the amir Kitbuqa, who was chief of the bakers.
And this Hulagu, [leaving] his son Jümghur
—who was from his chief queen—
with his mother in his place, in the service of Möngke Khan.
And this same son, after a time, when he set out to go abroad to his father,
passed away on the way.
Now he took with him from the rest of his sons:
his eldest son, whose name was Abaqa, and another son of his named Yoshmut.
And of the wives of Tolui Khan their father,
Doquz (Toquz?) Khatun, the faithful queen and true Christian,
was given to Hulagu as a wife according to the custom of the Mongols,
and she came with him.
And she exalted the horn of the Christians throughout all the earth.
Now they lingered on the way until the year six hundred and fifty-three of the Arabs (1255–1256 AD),
and then they reached Persia.
And in that same year, in the month of Tammuz (July),
suddenly an army of the Tatars attacked and came upon Melitene,
at whose head stood Yasawur, who had come against it eight years before.
And he took captive villages and hamlets,
and burned houses and threshing floors,
and killed whoever was found on his way,
and encamped on the northern side.
